implementation_notes: TypeScript's contribution is the type layer over facades the runtime already provides: the platform wraps the wire protocol (WebSocket, fetch) and node:fs surfaces FileHandle with Symbol.asyncDispose, so a facade is a thin class that owns the handle, exposes intent-named methods and implements Disposable/AsyncDisposable so callers get using/await using teardown - the explicit resource management support added in TypeScript 5.2. Type the boundary once and keep the runtime shim minimal; a declaration that describes behaviour the runtime does not have lies to every caller.
pitfalls: The WebSocket API has no backpressure: a facade that merely forwards send() buffers without bound when the peer is slow, so either expose flow control or use WebSocketStream.
Symbol.asyncDispose needs a runtime polyfill and lib esnext.disposable, otherwise await using compiles but throws at run time.
Types over a native addon must be re-checked per platform: a .d.ts that claims a method the prebuilt binary lacks fails only at run time.

variants.name: Typed facade over a Node-API addon
variants.idiom_name: hand-written .d.ts plus a thin wrapper module over the addon
variants.implementation_notes: When the wrapped API is a C library exposed through a Node-API addon, TypeScript supplies the missing half: a declaration file describing the native module's exports and a thin wrapper module that adds the invariants - a handle interface, one close path, input validation - on top of the untyped runtime. Keep the declarations next to the binary and derive them from the addon's actual exports, because the compiler cannot check the two against each other.
pitfalls: A declaration file is an unchecked assertion about the binary: drift between .d.ts and the addon's exports surfaces only at run time.
A Disposable implementation that never calls into the addon's close leaves the native handle alive even though the JavaScript object is gone.
The addon's own thread-safety and shutdown hooks sit outside the type system entirely and must be documented by the facade.
